# Chnobel autonomy

## When to Use
Use for development, recovery, review, CI and release continuation of Chnobel under its master prompt.

## Authority and startup
- Use `F:/Projects/Chnobel` for `mrdevn4ever-sys/learning-game-m`. Read its `MASTERPROMPT.md` in full and `steuerung/STATUS.md` at every restart, then applicable ADRs, task records and memory versions. The master prompt controls the scope; do not replace it with this abbreviated procedure.
- At `WARTEN`, perform no writes/uploads/optimisation; report `ABSCHLUSS.md`. At `BLOCKIERT_STARTPAKET`, verify that independent work really is exhausted and wait rather than inventing completion. Stop the project's continuation schedule at either valid terminal state.
- Honour an explicit user pause independently of completion: retain `ZUSTAND: IN_ARBEIT` and set `BETRIEB: PAUSIERT_AUF_NUTZERWUNSCH`, save `steuerung/WIEDERAUFNAHME.md` with exact branches/SHAs, evidence limits and next steps, verify the continuation cron is paused, and stop active review/worker contexts without treating partial results as verdicts. Do not resume on a limit reset, fresh session or late delegation delivery; require the user's explicit continuation. Check this latch before dispatching new work.
- Treat permission to resume as permission to continue the project, not to edit protected instruction files. Change AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or MASTERPROMPT.md only after explicit dialog approval; preserve an unapproved proposal as a hypothesis or ADR draft.
- Reconcile stopped or failed reviews from their delegation manifests, transcript terminal markers and expected report files before fresh dispatch. A rate-limit failure, interrupted context or missing/incomplete report is not a verdict, even when a plausible report or extensive partial files exist. Preserve and hash the partial inventory, restart in a fresh context against the exact unchanged candidate, and do not restart old implementation orders. Follow the user's ordered review/ratification/manifest/native stages rather than parallelising dependent stages.
- Limit Chnobel to at most two concurrent subagents. Split large consultations by question and technical specifications by independent section; retain the full required coverage in a persisted queue. A completed question shard is not a whole-role or whole-manifest verdict. Require complete, exact-version role votes before manifest approval and no implementation before the separate manifest gate.
- Before an actual interruption or imminent usage exhaustion, checkpoint STATUS, BLOCKER and WIEDERAUFNAHME, commit/push the owned documentation, read back remote SHAs and stop children cleanly. Do not start a large new review with a known insufficient budget. An asynchronous result handoff is not a pause: persist dispatched IDs and yield without polling or stopping those children.
- Keep runtime, virtual environments, caches, scratch and evidence on `F:/ChnobelRuntime`, outside Git. Git common directories also belong on F:. Use only this project's environments, never another project's interpreter/cache.

## Branches and independent roles
- Inspect actual branch, worktree status and live remote SHA before writes. Preserve in-flight workers and use separate F-backed worktrees with explicit path ownership.
- Product agents commit only their assigned source paths on workbranches. They never edit authoritative task states, merge, issue their own verdict or upload. The orchestrator applies reviewed transitions after independently rerunning tests.
- Require a different review context before merge. Context separation is not technical identity separation: the same account/token accessing product and private examination repositories cannot prove hidden-test isolation.
- Distinguish immutable review inputs from parent-owned handoff context when reviewers overlap checkpoint work. Bind normative text, cases, oracles and briefs before/after; separately record permitted STATUS/BLOCKER/WIEDERAUFNAHME changes with both hashes and their exact diff. A reviewer can observe an authorised intermediate parent patch rather than either whole commit: reconstruct that snapshot from its recorded diff and verify its raw hash. Compare Git-LF and worktree-CRLF separately, never call normalised equality raw-byte equality. Do not claim an atomic or unchanged whole read set or dismiss an unexplained normative drift as bookkeeping.
- Freeze every actually consumed procedural source, including skills and linked references, before dispatch; do not edit those sources while a bound reviewer is active. Keep their bindings separate from product norms and explicitly allowed mutable handoffs. If an extra procedural file drifts, preserve exact old/new bytes and reconstruct the recorded hashes, explain the cause without retroactive permission, retain the whole-readset exception, and bind the next reviewer to an explicit fresh procedural baseline without exposing peer recommendations.
- Reconcile repeated delegation deliveries by batch ID and archived content hashes before any transition. An unchanged already processed batch adds no vote and needs no redispatch. Inspect each role's actual metadata shape before checking conditions: field names can differ, so require the explicit unconditional flag and role-specific condition/text-change evidence rather than assuming one common key or silently defaulting a missing key.
- Ratify only complete, unconditional whole-document votes from distinct required roles bound to the exact frozen byte hash. Archive the voted draft, raw reports and votes losslessly before updating only ADR status/decision metadata; verify the normative text remains unchanged. Count votes mechanically, preserve dissent and defects, and keep a separate manifest-freeze/foreign-review gate before implementation. Product-policy ratification is not candidate, evidence, rights or release approval.
- Preserve Red-Team findings, failed candidate results and counts. After two repairs of the same cause, require a different hypothesis or independent reproduction. Never reduce gates, skip tests, empty a denominator or relabel earlier failures as passing.
- Record a later narrow technical acceptance in a separate hash-bound decision after verifying and losslessly preserving the complete foreign reviews. Keep the frozen proposal's historical unaccepted status unchanged. Resolve only the exact textual/source defect demonstrated fixed; separately track all retained inventory, acquisition, enforcement and whole-manifest integration obligations. A prescribed separate gate is neither an implemented service nor an executed success, and narrow acceptance cannot authorise product implementation.

## Public/private and Apple boundaries
- The product repository is public. Never put hidden cases/answers, archives, builds, IPA files, credentials or secret-bearing logs in it or its downloadable Actions artifacts. `chnobel-pruefung` is private, but privacy alone is not an ACL boundary.
- Public development CI must use minimal read permissions, no persisted checkout credentials, no secrets and only open synthetic regressions. Do not create successful dummy jobs for unavailable independent examination or release lanes.
- Privileged examination and release remain blocked until separate identities/ACLs, negative access tests, candidate sandboxing and a private artifact path are demonstrated. A name such as `PRUEFUNG_REPO_TOKEN` does not restrict its audience.
- The master prompt grants only TestFlight Internal Only. Do not create tester groups, invite people, attach to auto-distributing groups or submit to App Review/App Store release. Do not accept Apple contracts for the owner.
- Human-supplied secret values stay in protected service contexts. Inventory names only and do not repeat the once-issued human setup checklist each run. Continue all independent work.
- Before GitHub App registration, verify the actual signed-in browser owner against the repository owner; CLI authentication and an authenticated Chrome can belong to different accounts. Cancel an unsubmitted mismatched-owner form, inspect the account switcher, and keep registration blocked if the authorised owner is not already available. Never transfer a CLI credential into the browser or register under the wrong account.
- Reconcile environment writes even after HTTP errors: a rejected reviewer protection rule can still leave a newly created unprotected environment. Read the exact environment, branch/tag policies, secret-name inventory and Actions state; record partial configuration without calling it isolation. Do not infer the account plan or absence of every private environment feature from one unsupported protection rule.

## Evidence and product integrity
- Keep synthetic Python rules, Swift unit tests, iPad simulator/UI tests, hardware evidence and Apple processing separate. A current green run certifies only its exact source/artifacts and real executed counts.
- Before rerunning a returned worker suite, install that component's complete pinned requirements in the task-owned runtime, including JSON Schema format-checker plugins. Preserve an earlier dependency-failure run and record a fresh run after installation; do not weaken fail-closed validation or relabel the old result.
- Bind parent reruns to each exact clean worker commit and verify the remote SHA after checkpoint pushes. Aggregate counts programmatically, but never turn tests from separate branches into one integrated-candidate verdict. Keep native test definitions marked NOT RUN until macOS execution.
- Recognition proposals never become mathematical errors. Until real recognition exists, keep it explicitly disabled and the keypad reachable; synthetic fixtures are not a working CoreML recogniser. Never remove final handwriting acceptance requirements.
- Evaluate result, represented strategy, actor, material origin, assistance timing, undo and unknown separately. A fallback claim requires its own rule. Preserve narrow valid claims rather than silencing everything.
- Before native CI, verify live Apple upload requirements and runner image inventory. Pin the actual stable Xcode and select an available compatible iPad UDID. No public binary uploads as a convenience for evidence collection.
- For a diagnosis-only snapshot of rejected candidates, bind exact component trees and raw worktree bytes before push and execution; never import moving repair branches. Run a separate deterministic integration-veto job that verifies the archived review index, container/content digests and original FAIL candidate IDs. Keep native diagnosis independent of that veto, and preserve the draft PR and failed runs rather than issuing a new integration verdict.
- Bind native expected case counts and names before execution. SwiftPM can emit XCTest and Swift Testing xUnit files separately; validate the file belonging to the actual test definitions, not an empty XCTest aggregate. Require xcresult summary plus case identities for separate SwiftData/UI counts; reject suite-level errors even when case sums look positive. Preserve NOT RUN downstream stages after compiler failure and print source/run/toolchain-bound diagnostic counts without uploading builds.
- Inspect runtime-path guards before assigning a runner to controller recovery tests. A snapshot that requires an actual Windows F: path is not portable to Linux/macOS; a green local suite does not prove runner compatibility. Do not monkey-patch the guard or spoof a successful recovery. Keep the platform-contract failure distinct from native Swift errors and scope any future environment correction explicitly.
- Use Swiss spelling and no model/provider designations in product commits, code, content or reports. Existing source identifiers supplied by the owner remain literal; do not rewrite history to conceal them.

## Continuation handoff
- Update structured handoff files with targeted owned-field patches when the file tool marks a read as paginated; a wrapper's default read can retain that flag despite returning the full small file. After an overwrite refusal, preserve the incident and reuse already verified dispatch/archive artifacts instead of recreating them. Do not bypass write protection with an equivalent whole-file patch.
- Derive multiline patch search text from decoded raw bytes when the worktree uses CRLF; read_text() can silently normalise it to LF and defeat a long exact match. Preserve a refused edit, verify that nothing changed, then retry the same bounded section with its actual newline spelling rather than rewriting the whole file.
- Persist verified task state and next executable work before yielding. Keep leases/fencing and external operation IDs under deterministic control; reconcile uncertain uploads before any retry.
- If using cron, list existing project jobs first and keep only one continuation job. Do not overlap an active interactive writer. Fresh cron sessions must reread repository truth, not infer progress from a previous prose summary.
- Report concise German PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/open results tied to concrete evidence; never announce TestFlight-ready until every Definition-of-Done item and Apple's exact build status are verified.

# GitHub Pull Request Workflow

Complete guide for managing the PR lifecycle. Each section shows the `gh` way first, then the `git` + `curl` fallback.

## When to Use

Use for branch publication, documentation checkpoints, pull-request updates, CI diagnosis and authorised merges. Keep checkpoint publication separate from product acceptance; use the topical references for specialised verification recipes.

## Prerequisites

- Authenticated with GitHub (see `github-auth` skill)
- Inside a git repository with a GitHub remote

### Before touching an existing PR or pushing

1. Read repository instructions and `git status --short`; compare local HEAD with the PR head and remote branch. Preserve unrelated edits. If the requested checkout is missing, search likely locations first, then clone into a new directory rather than overwriting another working tree. If the repository has a narrow fetch refspec, a named `origin/*` ref may be absent **or stale even after `git fetch origin`**: compare `git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin "refs/heads/$BRANCH"` with `git rev-parse origin/$BRANCH`, fetch exactly `refs/heads/$BRANCH:refs/remotes/origin/$BRANCH`, and rerun SHA/ancestry gates on the refreshed ref before switching, pushing or declaring the source invalid. A narrow fetch updates only configured branches; an unrelated local branch with the same name is not a substitute for the live remote. If ordinary upstream setup rejects the explicitly fetched branch, set `branch.$BRANCH.remote=origin` and `branch.$BRANCH.merge=refs/heads/$BRANCH`, then compare local and remote SHAs; do not broaden the permanent fetchspec, conclude the branch is absent from local tracking state, or substitute another branch. For a main-preservation requirement, record the live remote main SHA before work and explicitly push only the named feature ref; do not amend commits merely to add a skip marker when the user requested an exact commit. If the remote feature branch advanced, inspect the new commits before integrating or editing—never overwrite them with force. Read back remote main after publication; if another actor changed it, report the difference rather than resetting it or claiming it remained identical.
2. Read the current PR body and draft/base/head state (`gh pr view <number> --json body,isDraft,baseRefName,headRefOid`). Update the existing PR without losing its useful context; distinguish **executed** tests from source-only checks and tests awaiting another OS/device.
3. If the user forbids CI usage, inspect `.github/workflows` on the target and default branches plus `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/workflows` **before** any push. Enumerate workflow paths at each exact commit before reading them: a feature-branch workflow may be absent from the default branch, and an API registration does not prove the file exists there. Record a verified empty YAML inventory separately from an unreadable or missing assumed filename. Do not start/enable workflows; use the requested `[skip ci]` commit marker, but do not treat it as a universal guarantee (other event types or external integrations may ignore it). **GitHub Pages triggers an Actions deployment even when publishing from a branch**: obtain explicit, narrowly scoped approval for **each proposed Pages push/deploy**, not just initial Pages setup. Check the Pages source and workflow triggers, then verify the exact new run completes and the live URLs serve the changed content (cache-busting if necessary). Keep this exception separate from app CI or upload permission. When triggers cannot be excluded, pause for a decision rather than spending minutes. After pushing, read back the exact PR head/body/draft state when a PR exists and query Actions for the exact published SHA as well as the branch. Reconcile `total_count` with the returned runs and pagination. Record empty results as a timestamped observation for those filters, not a permanent guarantee that no workflow can run.
4. Normally run the checks appropriate to the authorised scope, stage only owned files, run `git diff --cached --check`, and scan added lines for credential patterns before committing. For a documentation-only checkpoint, verify document bindings, lossless preservation and exact path ownership; do not start product tests, schema/evaluator execution or native builds merely to validate bookkeeping. Bind the gate result to the base commit and checked file hashes, recheck those bytes before staging, then require the staged path set to match the verified set exactly; otherwise an edit after the gate can enter an unchecked commit. Before consolidating review returns, inspect every role-specific record shape and the full required coverage set, then compare definitions and conditions as well as example values; matching finite matrices are not policy consensus. Keep document-check PASS, review recommendations, product acceptance and release authority separate. Before overlapping a review with checkpoint writes, bind two separate scopes: mutable context the reviewer may read, and exact parent-owned paths that may change. Neither permission implies the other, and neither permits changes to fixed review inputs. Keep hash-bound procedural sources, including skills and references, unchanged while dependent reviews are active; improve an unbound source or defer the edit rather than silently invalidating the review baseline. Use [review-document checkpoints](references/review-document-checkpoints.md) for the bounded inspection, preservation and publication recipe. If the owner explicitly orders an immediate checkpoint commit/push before verification, preserve that sequence: make the binary-safe, secret-scanned checkpoint, read back its remote SHA, then run the requested targeted and full suites, commit/push every fix, and create the PR only after the final gates pass. Label checkpoint publication separately from verified PR readiness. Never include secrets in output, commits, or PR text. A successful push is not proof that the PR description changed; edit and read it back separately.
5. For a manual GitHub Actions release from an unmerged PR, check GitHub's `workflow_dispatch` prerequisite **before promising an upload**: the workflow file must also exist on the default branch. Keep the app changes in the draft branch; get explicit permission before adding even a manual-only workflow to the default branch, and guard the default-branch job against accidental execution there. Distinguish permissions for the workflow-file push, billable runner minutes, and artifact upload. Inspect the workflow triggers before and after pushing—a manual-only workflow does not run merely because the branch was pushed. Dispatch with the intended `--ref` and inputs only after authorization, capture the run URL/ID returned by `gh workflow run`, and query that exact run ID for branch, head SHA, status and final conclusion. If a later jq/filter/discovery command fails after dispatch, verify the captured run instead of dispatching a duplicate. A queued or running dispatch is not proof of a signed build or uploaded artifact; do not launch extra diagnostic runs under a one-run approval.

6. Choose the **authorized release trigger** from the workflow at the exact source commit before pushing. Inspect `push` branch/tag/path filters, `git diff --name-status <old-target>..<source>`, live refs with `git ls-remote`, a clean worktree, required ancestor commits and target-as-ancestor-of-source with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`. A fast-forward branch push does **not** trigger a release limited to changes in a marker file when that file is unchanged. For an explicitly approved fast-forward route that *does* match the workflow filter, push only `origin/<source>:<target>` without force, tag or default-branch write, then read back the target and default branch SHAs.
   - When the owner instead authorizes initiating the build on the exact feature commit and the workflow documents a matching `push.tags` trigger, prefer one unique tag over an otherwise unnecessary merge plus marker commit. Check remote/local tag collisions and recent upload runs for that SHA; verify the live source SHA again, then `git tag <matching-name> <exact-sha>` and `git push origin refs/tags/<matching-name>:refs/tags/<matching-name>` without force. Read back the tag SHA. A tag selects that commit for the upload but does not advance the release branch; do not imply that it merged or start both trigger routes.
   - Find the resulting run by workflow, pushed ref and exact `headSha`; wait for its terminal conclusion. Inspect the export step and actual log for successful export/upload and the build number, not merely the badge or a workflow-authored success sentence. On failure report the failed step and relevant log excerpt without retrying the upload. If the owner explicitly prioritizes starting a non-corrective build while simulator tests remain pending, initiate the authorized release but label those tests unverified; read their conclusions once the upload run finishes and report `in_progress` honestly. Distinguish a green upload from Apple's processing, internal-group assignment and tester availability; report those as unverified unless independently read back.
   - If an older attempt's `gh run view --log` shows `UNKNOWN STEP`, use the attempt-specific jobs endpoint to verify the archive/export steps, then read that exact job's raw log. Match tool-emitted success and the actual archived build number (including the attempt suffix when used), not echoed shell commands. A known historical upload makes a positive verifier fixture; require it to fail for the current branch/SHA. This proves delivery only, not Apple processing.
7. When a feature depends on a separate test-harness correction, keep the production change and harness fix on separate branches. For local integration, overlay the exact dependency file at a recorded dependency SHA under a shell `trap` that restores it, run the complete gates, then verify the feature worktree has no harness diff. If combined review checks require a stacked PR, intentionally base the feature PR on the harness branch, state the dependency and retarget plan in the body, then retarget to the real base and rerun all gates after the harness merges. Never silently cherry-pick or commit the harness fix into the feature branch merely to make its suite pass.

### Independent-review checkpoints

- Record the reviewer's declared verdict separately from its eligibility under the governing review contract. Complete text coverage and matching hashes do not cure a missing mandatory evidence record. Preserve an ineligible opinion unchanged and obtain the required fresh-context review of the same frozen target; do not discard otherwise complete reviews merely because they retain documented tool failures.
- Keep current peer opinions out of every surface an independent reviewer may consume, including mutable status and handoff summaries. Put detailed vote accounting in controller-owned evidence outside that read scope; publish neutral progress in shared handoffs so checkpointing does not bias the remaining reviewers.
- For replacement review rounds, retain valid completed role votes and immutable original returns, bind the unchanged normative target separately from the new procedural baseline, and keep the project's concurrency and acceptance gates intact. A new dispatch is not a new acceptance decision.

### Cross-repository Xcode runner migrations

1. Enumerate the authenticated owner's non-archived repositories and inspect `.github/workflows` on each default branch **and active release/feature refs** (`gh repo list OWNER --limit 500`; `gh api 'repos/OWNER/REPO/contents/.github/workflows?ref=BRANCH'`). A workflow absent on `main` can still control a live release branch. Classify jobs by purpose; change only Apple/Xcode jobs, not Android, Linux, web, or unrelated Swift jobs.
2. Before editing, read every affected workflow's `push`, tag, path, `workflow_dispatch`, and `workflow_call` triggers plus the scripts it invokes. Verify the requested runner label, installed stable Xcode, SDK, simulator runtimes and device types against the current official runner-image inventory. `macos-latest` is not a major-Xcode pin; a new `runs-on` alone is insufficient when a helper still selects an older Xcode or requires an unavailable simulator/runtime. Preserve real device classes, StoreKit coverage, manual upload confirmations and secret gates; report an incompatible test as blocked instead of silently weakening it.
3. For large repositories, work in isolated partial/sparse clones rather than altering an active checkout. Limit the diff to workflows and necessary CI helpers; parse YAML without YAML 1.1 coercing `on` to a boolean, syntax-check extracted shell blocks, and inspect `git diff --check`. Before any push, recheck the exact remote ref and whether this commit can auto-run CI or release. Never trigger a signed upload merely to validate a runner migration.
4. After publication, read back each changed branch's remote SHA and the exact workflow files, then bind CI run IDs to that SHA. Report configuration, runner acquisition, SDK selection, native build/simulator tests, and TestFlight upload as separate states. If another active branch still has the old workflow, name it explicitly; a default-branch edit does not upgrade every release path.

### Quick Auth Detection

```bash
# Determine which method to use throughout this workflow
if command -v gh &>/dev/null && gh auth status &>/dev/null; then
  AUTH="gh"
else
  AUTH="git"
  # Ensure we have a token for API calls
  if [ -z "$GITHUB_TOKEN" ]; then
    if _hermes_env="${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/.env"; [ -f "$_hermes_env" ] && grep -q "^GITHUB_TOKEN=" "$_hermes_env"; then
      GITHUB_TOKEN=$(grep "^GITHUB_TOKEN=" "$_hermes_env" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2 | tr -d '\n\r')
    elif grep -q "github.com" ~/.git-credentials 2>/dev/null; then
      GITHUB_TOKEN=$(uv run python "${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/github/github-auth/scripts/git-credential-token.py")
    fi
  fi
fi
echo "Using: $AUTH"
```

### Extracting Owner/Repo from the Git Remote

Many `curl` commands need `owner/repo`. Extract it from the git remote:

```bash
# Works for both HTTPS and SSH remote URLs
REMOTE_URL=$(git remote get-url origin)
OWNER_REPO=$(echo "$REMOTE_URL" | sed -E 's|.*github\.com[:/]||; s|\.git$||')
OWNER=$(echo "$OWNER_REPO" | cut -d/ -f1)
REPO=$(echo "$OWNER_REPO" | cut -d/ -f2)
echo "Owner: $OWNER, Repo: $REPO"
```

---

## 1. Branch Creation

This part is pure `git` — identical either way:

```bash
# Only for a NEW branch and after confirming the working tree is clean:
git status --short
git fetch origin
git checkout main && git pull origin main

# Create and switch to a new branch
git checkout -b feat/add-user-authentication
```

Branch naming conventions:
- `feat/description` — new features
- `fix/description` — bug fixes
- `refactor/description` — code restructuring
- `docs/description` — documentation
- `ci/description` — CI/CD changes

## 2. Making Commits

Use the agent's file tools (`write_file`, `patch`) to make changes, then commit:

```bash
# Stage specific files
git add src/auth.py src/models/user.py tests/test_auth.py

# Commit with a conventional commit message
git commit -m "feat: add JWT-based user authentication

- Add login/register endpoints
- Add User model with password hashing
- Add auth middleware for protected routes
- Add unit tests for auth flow"
```

Commit message format (Conventional Commits):
```
type(scope): short description

Longer explanation if needed. Wrap at 72 characters.
```

Types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `ci`, `chore`, `perf`

## 3. Pushing and Creating a PR

### Push the Branch (same either way)

Only after the workflow-trigger gate above and a fresh remote-head check; never force-push over concurrent work. For a precautionary backup while another implementer is active, capture the exact existing commit SHA and push `<captured-sha>:refs/heads/<feature-branch>` rather than a moving `HEAD`; do not commit its in-progress edits, change branches or start another implementer. Skip a redundant push if that SHA is already remote. If CI use is prohibited, ensure the commit message carries `[skip ci]` and verify afterward that no Actions run started. When `gh` is authenticated and HTTPS Git would otherwise prompt, use the command-scoped helper `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git -c credential.helper= -c credential.helper='!gh auth git-credential' push origin <source>:refs/heads/<feature-branch>`; never export a token or change global credentials. Read back the exact branch with `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/<feature-branch>` before claiming it is backed up. PR head metadata can lag the branch immediately after a push: verify it separately, and do not issue a second push merely because the PR still shows its previous head.

```bash
git push -u origin HEAD
```

### Create the PR

**With gh:**

```bash
gh pr create \
  --title "feat: add JWT-based user authentication" \
  --body "## Summary
- Adds login and register API endpoints
- JWT token generation and validation

## Test Plan
- [ ] Unit tests pass

Closes #42"
```

Options: `--draft`, `--reviewer user1,user2`, `--label "enhancement"`, `--base develop`

**With git + curl:**

```bash
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)

curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.v3+json" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls \
  -d "{
    \"title\": \"feat: add JWT-based user authentication\",
    \"body\": \"## Summary\nAdds login and register API endpoints.\n\nCloses #42\",
    \"head\": \"$BRANCH\",
    \"base\": \"main\"
  }"
```

The response JSON includes the PR `number` — save it for later commands.

To create as a draft, add `"draft": true` to the JSON body.

## 4. Monitoring CI Status

- Budget sequential native test suites and device matrices before launching them; make the expected stages visible so a long test run is not mistaken for ongoing coding. Preserve required coverage, but avoid duplicate dispatches and repeated full runs for incidental edits. See [CI troubleshooting](references/ci-troubleshooting.md) for exact-stage inspection, elapsed-time accounting and cancellation diagnosis.
- Distinguish queued, running and completed jobs using the exact source SHA, job steps and conclusion. A watcher exit code or a long-running combined UI step alone does not identify a failing assertion, a specific active device, or a timeout. Do not advertise a successful build as successful UI acceptance.
- If one job has already completed but the overall run is still active, fetch that job's log directly with `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/jobs/JOB_ID/logs` and inspect the failing step; `gh run view --log-failed` can withhold logs until the entire run ends. Do not wait for unrelated long-running jobs before diagnosing an already-failed one.
- When a multi-commit delivery intentionally suppresses CI until the final media commit, verify that the final commit has no skip marker and changes a path matched by the intended workflow, then capture run IDs for that exact head SHA. If a follow-up commit supersedes a queued or running workflow, stop the stale local watcher without canceling the remote run unless authorized, discover the new SHA's runs, and report the old run as superseded. A green run for the previous SHA never verifies the new branch head. Treat late watcher notifications as evidence for their recorded SHA only, not as a reason to notify the user or start the next workflow. When promotion depends on independent checks, bind **each** prerequisite run ID, attempt and workflow to the same candidate SHA. Read each check's own verdict before the next dispatch and recheck the live branch head: a green functional run cannot override a failed benchmark, even if both Actions jobs show success. For a test-harness-only follow-up, verify its path scope and run the affected test lane; keep the performance failure attributed to the measured revision rather than treating the new SHA as a performance fix. Report when the current gate resolves or needs a decision, not each queue-to-runner transition.

- When a PR fails a deterministic regression test, run that exact shard on the clean base SHA with the same runtime and browser, then compare the failure signature. If base and PR fail identically, document the defect as pre-existing and move its repair to a separate branch/PR; never weaken the assertion. Treat it as a merge exception only when the owner explicitly authorizes that known baseline failure—local equivalence does not grant merge permission.

### Check CI Status

**With gh:**

```bash
# One-shot check
gh pr checks

# Watch until all checks finish (polls every 10s)
gh pr checks --watch
```

**With git + curl:**

```bash
# Get the latest commit SHA on the current branch
SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

# Query the combined status
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/commits/$SHA/status \
  | python -c "
import sys, json
data = json.load(sys.stdin)
print(f\"Overall: {data['state']}\")
for s in data.get('statuses', []):
    print(f\"  {s['context']}: {s['state']} - {s.get('description', '')}\")"

# Also check GitHub Actions check runs (separate endpoint)
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/commits/$SHA/check-runs \
  | python -c "
import sys, json
data = json.load(sys.stdin)
for cr in data.get('check_runs', []):
    print(f\"  {cr['name']}: {cr['status']} / {cr['conclusion'] or 'pending'}\")"
```

### Poll Until Complete (git + curl)

```bash
# Simple polling loop — check every 30 seconds, up to 10 minutes
SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  STATUS=$(curl -s \
    -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
    https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/commits/$SHA/status \
    | python -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['state'])")
  echo "Check $i: $STATUS"
  if [ "$STATUS" = "success" ] || [ "$STATUS" = "failure" ] || [ "$STATUS" = "error" ]; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 30
done
```

## 5. Auto-Fixing CI Failures

When CI fails, diagnose and fix. This loop works with either auth method.

### Step 1: Get Failure Details

**With gh:**

```bash
# List recent workflow runs on this branch
gh run list --branch $(git branch --show-current) --limit 5

# View failed logs
gh run view <RUN_ID> --log-failed
```

**With git + curl:**

```bash
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)

# List workflow runs on this branch
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/runs?branch=$BRANCH&per_page=5" \
  | python -c "
import sys, json
runs = json.load(sys.stdin)['workflow_runs']
for r in runs:
    print(f\"Run {r['id']}: {r['name']} - {r['conclusion'] or r['status']}\")"

# Get failed job logs (download as zip, extract, read)
RUN_ID=<run_id>
curl -s -L \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/logs \
  -o /tmp/ci-logs.zip
cd /tmp && unzip -o ci-logs.zip -d ci-logs && cat ci-logs/*.txt
```

### Step 2: Fix and Push

After identifying the issue, use file tools (`patch`, `write_file`) to fix it:

```bash
git add <fixed_files>
git commit -m "fix: resolve CI failure in <check_name>"
git push
```

### Step 3: Verify

Re-check CI status using the commands from Section 4 above.

### Auto-Fix Loop Pattern

When asked to auto-fix CI, follow this loop:

1. Check CI status → identify failures
2. Read failure logs → understand the error
3. Use `read_file` + `patch`/`write_file` → fix the code
4. Stage the specific owned files, check the staged diff, then commit and push only if the user's CI policy allows it; never use `git add .` on an existing working tree.
5. When CI is authorized, wait for it and re-check status; otherwise report only the locally executed checks.
6. Repeat only within the owner's remaining retry budget (up to 3 attempts by default when no stricter limit was set). Count a dispatched run or rerun even when it fails; an explicit one-run allowance does not renew after diagnosis or a local fix. Exhaust the authorized read-only investigation and local checks, then ask for renewed native/CI permission before another dispatch.

## 6. Merging

A branch push or PR-creation request does not authorize merge, auto-merge, branch deletion or deployment. If the owner says not to merge, stop after the PR and required check readback even when every gate is green.

**With gh:**

```bash
# Squash merge + delete branch (cleanest for feature branches)
gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch

# Enable auto-merge (merges when all checks pass)
gh pr merge --auto --squash --delete-branch
```

**With git + curl:**

```bash
PR_NUMBER=<number>

# Merge the PR via API (squash)
curl -s -X PUT \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/merge \
  -d "{
    \"merge_method\": \"squash\",
    \"commit_title\": \"feat: add user authentication (#$PR_NUMBER)\"
  }"

# Delete the remote branch after merge
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)
git push origin --delete $BRANCH

# Switch back to main locally
git checkout main && git pull origin main
git branch -d $BRANCH
```

Merge methods: `"merge"` (merge commit), `"squash"`, `"rebase"`

### Enable Auto-Merge (curl)

```bash
# Auto-merge requires the repo to have it enabled in settings.
# This uses the GraphQL API since REST doesn't support auto-merge.
PR_NODE_ID=$(curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER \
  | python -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['node_id'])")

curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/graphql \
  -d "{\"query\": \"mutation { enablePullRequestAutoMerge(input: {pullRequestId: \\\"$PR_NODE_ID\\\", mergeMethod: SQUASH}) { clientMutationId } }\"}"
```
